label: late original-phase v/d/c/l/i/digit inputs in sequences starting with f/n/j-like letters
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase, which holds 98% of activation mass. It needs orig_idx >= 3 and peaks at positions 4-7. It is driven by the current input: v, d, c and l give the highest rates (4-7x lift), then i, 3, 2 and x. Sequence history modulates it strongly: the rate is much higher when the first token, or earlier tokens, are f, n or j (also g, z, p, e, b). The top examples are all f/n/j-heavy prefixes followed by d/v/c/i. It is mostly a first occurrence of the input token (87% of mass). It is essentially silent at t = 0-1, at the delimiter, and in the copy phase (2% of mass, mostly recall_idx 1 when outputting f). Precision is weak (about 0.4): the same input tokens at late positions with an f/n/j-type start often do not fire. The unit looks like a graded function of the accumulated prefix plus the current input, not a crisp condition. Magnitude rises with position up to about 5-6 and with f/n/j content in the prefix; this was checked against the top examples and the per-position mass tables.
